History:
- Presenting complaint: Low mood, decreased appetite, low energy, intermittent palpitations, and nausea.
- Onset/duration/progression:
  - Low mood, low energy, and decreased appetite for several months; patient reports symptoms began after changing to a new law firm ~3–3.5 months ago but some weight loss preceded that (~6 months).
  - Weight loss ~1 stone over approximately 6 months.
  - Intermittent nausea, not associated with vomiting or specific foods.
  - Palpitations and shortness of breath described particularly when in lifts; patient reports no chest pain with these episodes.
  - Can walk about a mile without shortness of breath (patient later states he has not been walking recently, making assessment harder).
- Associated symptoms/negatives:
  - Headaches reported intermittently.
  - No cough, no diarrhea, no blood or mucus in stool, no vomiting.
  - Bowel motions described as painless and otherwise normal.
  - No current thyroid blood tests; patient stopped taking thyroxine some time ago.

Past Medical History:
- Underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism).
- Medications: Thyroxine — dose/route/frequency not documented; patient reports he has not taken it since changing doctors.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Prior investigations/hospitalizations: No recent blood tests; no other hospitalizations documented.

Physical Examination:
- No formal physical examination documented during this consult.
- Patient-reported/observed findings:
  - Alert and conversational.
  - Low mood and low energy.
  - Intermittent palpitations (patient feels heart racing), especially in lifts.
  - No chest pain reported.
  - No cough.
  - No vomiting.
  - Reports reduced appetite and ~1 stone weight loss.
- Relevant negatives:
  - No throat swelling mentioned.
  - No diarrheal stools, no blood/mucus in stool.

Impression:
- Low mood with decreased appetite and energy for months, associated with ~1 stone weight loss and intermittent palpitations; history of hypothyroidism with recent cessation of thyroxine — thyroid dysfunction and metabolic causes to be investigated.

Management Plan:
- Immediate actions advised:
  - Arrange a general set of blood tests to investigate causes (doctor stated they will look for anemia, kidney function, liver function, and vitamin levels).
  - Patient instructed to call the support number in the app (an 03xx number) so staff can organize blood tests.
  - If patient develops chest pain or severe palpitations, advised to go to A&E as an emergency.
  - If bowel habits change or vomiting occurs, advised to contact the service promptly.
- Follow-up/advice:
  - After blood results are available the patient will receive a text message instructing him to book a follow-up appointment.
  - If blood tests are normal, a physical examination will be arranged subsequently.
  - Patient advised to recontact sooner if symptoms worsen.

Patient Summary (2–3 lines):
- Patient Peter Peterson reports several months of low mood, decreased appetite, low energy, intermittent nausea, ~1 stone weight loss over ~6 months, and palpitations mainly in lifts. He has a history of hypothyroidism but stopped taking thyroxine after changing doctors and has not had recent blood tests. Plan is to arrange general blood tests (anemia, renal, liver, vitamin levels) via support; follow-up appointment will be arranged after results, and urgent A&E if chest pain develops.

Key Takeaways:
- Call the support number in the app to arrange the blood tests.
- Attend A&E urgently for chest pain or severe palpitations.
- Contact the service if bowel habits change or if vomiting develops.

Next Steps:
- Support team to organize general blood tests (to evaluate anemia, kidney and liver function, and vitamin levels) — patient to call the app support number to initiate.
- Receive text notification to book follow-up once blood results are available.
- If blood tests are normal, schedule and perform a physical examination and further assessment.
- Reassess medication (thyroxine) and consider re-initiation only after review of blood results and clinical assessment.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies: not documented.
  - Complete medication reconciliation (other regular medications, OTCs, supplements) not documented.
  - Vital signs and physical examination findings not documented.
  - Exact blood tests ordered and timing not explicitly listed; thyroid function test not explicitly documented though clinical history suggests relevance.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Duration of symptoms: patient alternately states onset ~3–3.5 months since job change and also reports some weight loss over a longer period (~6 months).
  - Exercise/SOB assessment conflict: patient reports he can walk ~1 mile without SOB but later states he has not been walking recently so it is hard to identify when shortness of breath occurs.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally intelligible with occasional brief inaudible segments and interruptions; some sentences incomplete or trailing off, but overall sufficient for clinical summary.
